Maria C: Quick heads-up — saw a sharp drop in prefix cache hit-rate on the private cluster after yesterday's kernel-selection change. Profiling attached below.
Sam R: What numbers are we seeing? Hosted/dedicated/private split?
Maria C: Baseline (before change): dedicated ~0.95, hosted ~0.86, private ~0.82. After change: dedicated ~0.92, hosted ~0.68, private ~0.60. This is for our 8k-seq conversational workload during peak.
Priya N: Oof. Any obvious regression signal from the kernel selection heuristics? Which fallback was flipped?
Maria C: The change biased toward the new low-memory GEMM path for attention when seq_len < 2048, to reduce p50 on small batch inference. That reduced single-call memory but increased per-token latency for longer prefixes in some configs.
Alex T: How does that affect cache hit-rate though? Sounds like a compute micro-regression, not cache.
Maria C: It's interactional. Two effects we instrumented:
 - Batching heuristics: increased per-token latency causes the batching controller to cut batch wait windows to keep p50 SLO; fewer coalesced requests -> fewer shared prefix opportunities -> lower observed hit-rate.
 - Network-backed KV store behavior: private clusters use NFS-style filestore (mount: nfs://cachefs) with slightly higher metadata RTT. When batches shrink, more KV gets fetched concurrently, exposing mount latency and dirent TTL (we saw extra metadata calls).
Leo M: Do we have traces? p99 numbers?
Maria C: Short snippet from perf agent:
```
Before: p50=28ms p95=120ms p99=260ms, hit-rate=0.82
After:  p50=33ms p95=210ms p99=520ms, hit-rate=0.60
Throughput tokens/s: 240k -> 170k
```
infra-bot: deploy:kernel-fallback-v2 rolled in region-dc-3 at 2026-11-02T02:14:12Z
Sam R: Interesting that dedicated barely moved. I guess because dedicated uses local NVMe cache shards + in-process KV which masks the per-request overhead.
Priya N: Can we isolate whether the KV keying changed? Any normalization difference between hosted/dedicated/private configs?
Maria C: We checked — keying (prefix normalization) unchanged. But we did find a subtle path: private path uses a different canonicalization codepath that adds a truncated sha256 suffix for long prompts. That increased key length and triggered a slower lookup path in our filestore client (extra UTF-8 normalization). Happened to be N rare cases, but with more tiny batches it amplified.
Alex T: Remediation candidates?
Maria C: Short list we discussed:
 1) Revert kernel fallback until batching heuristics are tuned.
 2) Increase batching window for longer seq workloads in private/hosted (config override per deployment type).
 3) Patch filestore client to skip redundant normalization on canonicalized keys and add a small positive cache for dirent metadata (TTL 10s).
 4) Add a proactive warmup job in private: a background worker that issues common prefixes at low QPS to keep KV shards hot and amortize dirent RTT.
Leo M: Any SQL / commands for reproducing locally?
Maria C: Repro script we used (shortened):
```
# simulate 8k seq traffic with prefix reuse
python tools/sim_traffic.py --seq 8192 --pattern conversational --qps 120 --affinity private
# run perf collector
curl -s http://localhost:8080/internal/perf > /tmp/perf.json
```
Sam R: Who wants to own the quick patch to filestore client? I can take batching heuristics tuning.
Priya N: I can do the warmup worker and a short experiment to raise batching window in private for 24h and report hit-rate.
Maria C: Perfect. Action items:
 - Sam R: tune batching window and adjust coalescing threshold (T+6h)
 - Priya N: implement warmup worker + run 24h canary in private (T+12h)
 - Alex T: small patch to filestore client to bypass duplicate normalization (PR + perf test, T+24h)
 - Infra: hold off on full region-wide rollout of kernel-fallback until we have canary numbers (infra-bot: please pause further rollouts)
infra-bot: action:rollback-scheduled kernel-fallback-v2 -> paused by infra on request of @Maria C
Maria C: Thanks team. Please post perf deltas and one-line summary in this thread when you have results. :thumbsup:
Sam R: Will update. Low-effort mitigation first: bump batching window from 6ms -> 12ms for private and monitor hit-rate.
Priya N: Starting warmup worker now on canary-private-1. Will tag logs with warmup:key:* so we can filter.
Alex T: PR opened for filestore client: https://git.redwood/infrastore/PR/4287 — simple fastpath for already-canonical keys. Running unit + perf.
Leo M: Logging a short postmortem note in eng-runtime/postmortems after we verify fixes. Good catch catching the interaction effects early.
Maria C: Summary for the thread: regression is an emergent interaction between kernel-selection micro-optimization + batching heuristics + network-backed KV path and key canonicalization differences across deployment types. Fix plan = batching tweak + filestore fastpath + warmup job.
